scope: Crime and punishment, fines, bounties, notoriety, Interstellar Factors, detention, mission rewards, Team/Wing mission sharing, massacre stacking, illegal missions, and mission-selection workflow used by the Mongrels Field Manual and Ask the Mongrels.

entries.ruleOfThumb: Treat fines, bounties and notoriety as separate layers. Fines are minor legal debts, bounties create Wanted status in the relevant jurisdiction, and notoriety is a CMDR-wide murder penalty that can block legal cleanup.
details: A fine by itself is not the same as a bounty and does not normally make the ship Wanted.
A bounty makes the offending ship Wanted in jurisdictions where that bounty is valid.
Notoriety is separate from the ship's bounty and is attached to the commander.
Outstanding legal issues can restrict station services through Anonymous Access at ports tied to the issuing faction or jurisdiction.

sources.name: Frontier Forums — current crime/legal-system discussion
Elite Dangerous Wiki — Crime & Punishment

entries.ruleOfThumb: Pay ordinary fines through an appropriate Authority Contact when possible. If the fine will not appear locally, use an Interstellar Factor in a system where the issuing faction is not present.
details: Fines are lower-level legal penalties and generally do not create Wanted status on their own.
A fine can still trigger Anonymous Access or restricted services at affected ports until resolved.
If a fine refuses to appear at a contact, a menu relog can sometimes refresh stale legal-state data.
Interstellar Factors can clear remote fines when their normal eligibility conditions are met.

sources.name: INARA community — current Interstellar Factors/fine behavior
Frontier Forums — Interstellar Factor discussion

entries.ruleOfThumb: A bounty is tied to the offending ship's legal record, so use that ship when clearing it. If notoriety is zero, either use a qualifying Interstellar Factor or hand yourself in to the issuing authority.
details: Ship bounties persist until paid, claimed or otherwise resolved.
Because legal records are ship-specific, changing ships can make the problem appear to vanish even though the offending ship still carries the bounty.
Interstellar Factors are usually the convenient option when the bounty-issuing faction is not present at the Factor's location.
Turning yourself in clears eligible bounties but relocates you to a detention facility.

sources.name: Frontier Forums — bounty cleanup and ship-specific legal state
Frontier Forums — current legal-system discussion

entries.ruleOfThumb: If notoriety is above zero, stop committing murders and remain logged into the game while it decays. The established decay rate is one point per two hours of active game time.
details: Notoriety rises from serious criminal kills and can reach 10.
Decay requires active logged-in game time; logging out pauses it.
Interstellar Factors will not clear relevant bounties while notoriety remains above zero.
Notoriety is commander-wide rather than tied to a single ship.

quickFacts.label: Decay
quickFacts.value: 1 point per 2 hours active game time

sources.name: Elite Dangerous Wiki — Notoriety

entries.ruleOfThumb: Use an Interstellar Factor for remote legal cleanup only after notoriety reaches zero, and preferably choose a system where the issuing faction is not present.
details: Interstellar Factors provide centralized access to remote fines/bounties and redemption services.
The issuing faction's presence can prevent a fine or bounty from appearing at that Factor; use a different system if needed.
Interstellar Factors add a 25% service fee to legal payments and deduct 25% from eligible voucher redemptions.
If a valid transaction does not appear, a menu relog can sometimes refresh the legal state.

sources.name: Frontier Forums — current Interstellar Factor guidance
INARA community — Interstellar Factor 25% fee

entries.ruleOfThumb: Turning yourself in is the direct-authority route for clearing an eligible bounty, but expect to be transported to a detention facility rather than remaining at the original station.
details: At zero notoriety, the Authority/Security Contact can offer a turn-yourself-in option for qualifying bounties.
This resolves the bounty and moves the commander to a detention facility.
Use Interstellar Factors instead when you want to avoid the detention transfer and meet their eligibility rules.
Detention facilities provide core ship services so you can recover and depart after processing.

entries.topic: Mission Board Access, Reputation & Better Offers
entries.ruleOfThumb: Build reputation with the mission-giving minor faction if you want better access and stronger payouts. Allied factions generally offer the best mission selection.
details: Mission availability and payout are influenced by your reputation with the issuing minor faction.
Relevant Pilots Federation career rank can also affect mission generation and reward quality.
If you are farming a mission type, becoming Allied with several local factions improves the board substantially.
Do not confuse minor-faction reputation with the faction's system influence percentage; they are separate values.

sources.name: Frontier Forums — developer explanation of reputation/influence reward scaling
INARA community — mission progression example

entries.topic: Credits, Reputation, Influence & Material Reward Choices
entries.ruleOfThumb: Choose rewards for the objective: REP to build standing or superpower progression, INF for BGS work, materials for engineering bottlenecks, and credits when none of those matter more.
details: REP rewards increase your reputation with the mission-giving faction and can support aligned superpower rank progression where applicable.
INF rewards increase the mission's BGS influence effect for the issuing faction; the plus signs indicate relative reward strength.
Engineering-material rewards can be extremely valuable after the 2024 rebalance, with some missions offering much larger quantities than older guides show.
Credit-maximizing is not always the best choice when working squad BGS or building Engineer-material reserves.

sources.name: Frontier Forums — developer explanation of REP/INF plus ratings
Frontier — Type-8 Update / mission-material rebalance

entries.ruleOfThumb: For Team/Wing missions, share the mission and have squadmates accept it before turn-in. After completion, non-owner participants collect their reward from the issuing location within the claim window.
details: Only missions explicitly designed for Team/Wing sharing should be treated as shareable mission contracts.
Coordinate before turn-in so every intended participant has accepted the shared mission.
Participants who did not own the mission receive a completion message directing them where to collect the reward.
Community and journal behavior document a 30-day window for invited participants to collect completed shared-mission rewards.

sources.name: INARA community — Team/Wing sharing workflow
INARA — shared mission reward collection behavior

entries.ruleOfThumb: Pirate massacre kills stack when missions targeting the same enemy faction come from different issuing factions. Multiple missions from the same issuing faction generally serialize rather than sharing each kill.
details: The useful setup is several source factions all offering pirate massacres against the same target faction.
A qualifying kill can advance one mission from each different issuing faction at the same time.
Taking many same-faction massacre contracts does not multiply progress in the same way.
Colonization can change which nearby systems generate missions, so use a current mission-source tool rather than relying on old farming locations.

sources.name: INARA — Flat Galaxy Society massacre guide
Frontier Forums — massacre stacking mechanics
INARA — 2025 massacre-source search update

entries.ruleOfThumb: A mission objective does not automatically make every target legal to kill. Check whether the individual is Wanted in the current jurisdiction and whether the mission itself is marked illegal.
details: Legal pirate targets can usually be killed without creating a criminal record once their Wanted status is confirmed.
Illegal assassination and covert missions can deliberately require crimes and may generate fines, bounties or notoriety depending on what you do.
On-foot and ship missions can contain legal and illegal variants with similar-looking objectives.
When doing squad BGS work, account for both the mission reward and any criminal actions performed during completion.

sources.name: Frontier Forums — current legal-system mission discussion
Frontier Forums — Crime & mission-target discussion

entries.ruleOfThumb: Read the failure consequences before accepting. Mission failure or abandonment can reduce reputation, create BGS consequences, and impose financial penalties—especially when mission cargo or special items were issued to you.
details: Penalty size and type vary by mission template, so do not assume every abandoned mission is harmless.
Failing missions for a faction damages reputation with that faction and can be relevant to BGS operations.
Cargo-delivery and source missions can impose fines or losses when issued mission cargo is not returned or delivered as required.
Mission timers continue to matter even when the objective itself has already consumed significant travel or combat time.

sources.name: INARA community — BGS effects of mission failure

entries.topic: Illegal / Stolen Cargo and Mission Scans
entries.ruleOfThumb: Illegal or stolen cargo becomes a legal-risk problem when scanned in a jurisdiction that prohibits it. Plan the route and destination before accepting smuggling or theft-related work.
details: Illegal cargo and stolen cargo are not identical labels, but both can create fines or other legal consequences when detected in the wrong jurisdiction.
Black Markets are used to sell many illegal or stolen commodities where accepted.
Silent running, heat management and avoiding scans are operational tools, but they do not erase the legal status of the cargo.
Mission-specific cargo may be unique to the contract and should not be treated like ordinary market stock.

sources.name: INARA community — black markets / illegal trade discussion

entries.topic: Choosing Missions for Credits, Materials, Rank or BGS
entries.ruleOfThumb: Pick missions by objective, not by headline credit value. Credits, engineering materials, reputation, superpower rank and BGS influence often point to different optimal choices.
details: For engineering progression, prioritize hard-to-source material rewards even when the credit payout is lower.
For reputation or naval-rank work, favor strong REP rewards from aligned factions.
For squad BGS, take missions for the intended faction and select the highest useful INF reward while respecting operational orders and stop conditions.
For raw credits, Team/Wing cargo and massacre missions can scale well when coordinated, but they should not override BGS instructions in squad-controlled systems.
